# La Turbine Sciences – Key Details

**Prices/Tarifs:**
- Adults: €5.50
- Under 18 years: €3.00
- Under 6 years: Free
- Group visits: €60 per visit or €100 for 2 visits in one day

**Opening Hours:**
"Tue-Sun 14h-18h · closed Mondays and public holidays · groups Tue-Fri 9h or 10:30 on reservation"

**Address:**
Place Chorus / 3 rue des Tisserands, 74960 Annecy (Cran-Gevrier), Haute-Savoie, France

**Indoor & Family-Suitable:**
Yes. This is an indoor science center housed in a rehabilitated former paper mill. It features interactive exhibitions, a digital planetarium, and workshops. The venue offers "manipulations ludiques" (playful hands-on activities) covering topics like optical illusions, physics, and biology—designed for children from age 4 upward. During school holidays, mediated workshops run 1-2 hours. The facility is fully wheelchair accessible and holds the "Tourisme & Handicap" label for motor and mental accessibility.

**Visit Duration:** Typically 1–2 hours (up to half-day with planetarium and workshops)

Researched loisirs74.fr (read-only — browsed the category listings and venue pages, no forms or bookings). Here's a rainy-afternoon plan.

## The three picks

**1. La Turbine sciences** — Place Chorus / 3 rue des Tisserands, Cran-Gevrier (Annecy)
Interactive science centre in a former paper mill: hands-on physics/optics/biology exhibits, digital planetarium, holiday workshops. Designed from age 4 up, fully wheelchair accessible (Tourisme & Handicap label).
- Adults **€5.50** · under 18 **€3.00** · under 6 **free**
- Groups €60/visit, or €100 for two visits in a day
- Tue–Sun 14h–18h, closed Mondays and public holidays

**2. Patinoire Jean Régis** — 27 rue du Stade, Annecy
Covered 58×28 m municipal rink, open year-round. Free on-site parking.
- Adults **€4.60** + **€3.40** skate rental · children **€3.00**
- Public sessions Wed/Sat/Sun 14h–18h; daily during school holidays; Friday 20h–23h disco (too late for young kids)

**3. Le Bowl** — 9 boulevard du Fier, Annecy
16 lanes plus a restaurant, so it doubles as the dinner stop. Free parking.
- **€8** per game (adult) · **€6** per game (child); family evening packages exist
- Open from 14h daily (to 1h Mon–Thu, 4h Fri–Sat, midnight Sun); 30–45 min per game
- The page doesn't list a shoe-rental price — worth checking on arrival

## Suggested afternoon

Pick a **Wednesday, Saturday or Sunday** — that's the overlap where all three are open.

- **14h00–16h00** La Turbine (it opens at 14h and shuts at 18h, so go first)
- **16h30–18h00** Patinoire Jean Régis — 10 min away, catches the tail of the public session
- **18h30** Le Bowl, one game then eat on site

If you'd rather not do two timed 14h–18h venues back-to-back, swap the skating for the **Musée-Château d'Annecy** (1 place du Château): **€6.50** full price Sept–June (€7.00 in July–Aug), reduced €3.50/€4.00, **under 12s free**, closed Tuesdays. A combined ticket with the Palais de l'Île is €8.00 (€9.00 in summer).

## Rough cost, 2 adults + 2 children (ages 6–17)

| Venue | Cost |
|---|---|
| La Turbine | €17.00 |
| Patinoire (incl. 4 skate rentals) | €28.80 |
| Le Bowl (1 game each) | €28.00 |
| **Total** | **€73.80** |

Swapping the rink for the Musée-Château drops it to about €58 (kids under 12 free there).

Two caveats worth passing on: these are the 2026 tariffs as published on loisirs74.fr, and the site itself flags some figures as estimates pending confirmation — that's why I skipped **Bam Freesports** (trampoline park, Zone d'activité de Vovray) as a main pick, since its page only gives "~12–16 € per hour session" plus ~€3 for compulsory grip socks. It's a good backup if you want something more physical, but confirm the price directly. Also, the venue pages recommend booking ahead for weekends and school holidays — I haven't reserved anything.

entries.text:
Researched loisirs74.fr (read-only — browsed the category listings and venue pages, no forms or bookings). Here's a rainy-afternoon plan.

## The three picks

**1. La Turbine sciences** — Place Chorus / 3 rue des Tisserands, Cran-Gevrier (Annecy)
Interactive science centre in a former paper mill: hands-on physics/optics/biology exhibits, digital planetarium, holiday workshops. Designed from age 4 up, fully wheelchair accessible (Tourisme & Handicap label).
- Adults **€5.50** · under 18 **€3.00** · under 6 **free**
- Groups €60/visit, or €100 for two visits in a day
- Tue–Sun 14h–18h, closed Mondays and public holidays

**2. Patinoire Jean Régis** — 27 rue du Stade, Annecy
Covered 58×28 m municipal rink, open year-round. Free on-site parking.
- Adults **€4.60** + **€3.40** skate rental · children **€3.00**
- Public sessions Wed/Sat/Sun 14h–18h; daily during school holidays; Friday 20h–23h disco (too late for young kids)

**3. Le Bowl** — 9 boulevard du Fier, Annecy
16 lanes plus a restaurant, so it doubles as the dinner stop. Free parking.
- **€8** per game (adult) · **€6** per game (child); family evening packages exist
- Open from 14h daily (to 1h Mon–Thu, 4h Fri–Sat, midnight Sun); 30–45 min per game
- The page doesn't list a shoe-rental price — worth checking on arrival

## Suggested afternoon

Pick a **Wednesday, Saturday or Sunday** — that's the overlap where all three are open.

- **14h00–16h00** La Turbine (it opens at 14h and shuts at 18h, so go first)
- **16h30–18h00** Patinoire Jean Régis — 10 min away, catches the tail of the public session
- **18h30** Le Bowl, one game then eat on site

If you'd rather not do two timed 14h–18h venues back-to-back, swap the skating for the **Musée-Château d'Annecy** (1 place du Château): **€6.50** full price Sept–June (€7.00 in July–Aug), reduced €3.50/€4.00, **under 12s free**, closed Tuesdays. A combined ticket with the Palais de l'Île is €8.00 (€9.00 in summer).

## Rough cost, 2 adults + 2 children (ages 6–17)

| Venue | Cost |
|---|---|
| La Turbine | €17.00 |
| Patinoire (incl. 4 skate rentals) | €28.80 |
| Le Bowl (1 game each) | €28.00 |
| **Total** | **€73.80** |

Swapping the rink for the Musée-Château drops it to about €58 (kids under 12 free there).

Two caveats worth passing on: these are the 2026 tariffs as published on loisirs74.fr, and the site itself flags some figures as estimates pending confirmation — that's why I skipped **Bam Freesports** (trampoline park, Zone d'activité de Vovray) as a main pick, since its page only gives "~12–16 € per hour session" plus ~€3 for compulsory grip socks. It's a good backup if you want something more physical, but confirm the price directly. Also, the venue pages recommend booking ahead for weekends and school holidays — I haven't reserved anything.
